exhibit-1.summary: The funnel table steps from US adults through the disease, diagnosis, treatment and severity stages to eligible patients, with Aldermoor's forecast peak share and Kelvexa's list price, rebates and time on treatment.

exhibit-2.summary: The specialist survey lists the reasons to prescribe Kelvexa and the barriers to prescribing it, each with the share of specialists naming it.

exhibit-3.summary: The entry options table compares building Aldermoor's own US team with partnering: who sells, what Aldermoor receives, who pays the selling costs, the expected peak share and the time to launch.

definitions.text: US adults times the share of adults who have Corlan's disease.
US adults with Corlan's disease who are diagnosed, treated with prescription medicine and moderate-to-severe; each funnel rate applies to the stage above it.
Eligible patients times Aldermoor's forecast peak share of eligible patients.
Kelvexa's list price less the average discounts and rebates to insurers, per patient per year.
Patients on Kelvexa at peak times the net price per patient per year; net sales are revenue after discounts and rebates.
The board's peak sales threshold divided by the net price per patient per year.
The patients needed to reach the board's threshold, as a share of eligible patients.
Peak net sales scale in proportion to the diagnosis rate when the other funnel rates and the peak share stay the same.
Under Option A Aldermoor keeps all US net sales and pays the annual US selling costs, so its profit at peak is peak net sales less those selling costs.
Eligible patients times the expected peak share with a partner times the net price per patient per year.
Aldermoor's royalty rate times the US net sales under Option B; the partner pays the selling costs.
The share of eligible patients at which Option A's profit equals Option B's: Option B's profit plus Option A's selling costs, divided by the net price, as a share of eligible patients.

mustReach.why: Proposed: the candidate never hears what the US standard therapy is, yet Exhibit 2 rates Kelvexa against 'current options' and the coverage line names Nimbrel. Missed in 4 of 15 Aldermoor runs, never released through the end of the run (recommendation included): b32 Jasmine (40, 6544aa01; Exhibit 2 at t8); b34 Jasmine (40, 4e89a7cc; Exhibit 2 at t6; hand grade: serious false refusal t4, never heard of Nimbrel); b34 Marisol (57, a1133734; Exhibit 2 at t14, 'Nimbrel is covered by most plans' at t16 to a candidate never told what Nimbrel is, hand grade; serious false refusal t14); b36 Jasmine (40, 6bbc2163; Exhibit 2 at t8). Late in a fifth: b36 Marisol (57, 6f57da6e; Exhibit 2 at t12, the coverage line naming Nimbrel at t14, nimbrel only at t16; hand grade notes the recurrence).

proposed.note: Lorenzo's ruling (22 Oct): Aldermoor must-reach goes in proposed only, with its justifying runs. One proposal: nimbrel before exhibit-2. Alternative if he prefers the Hollis Bay/Quillpath form: nimbrel before recommendation (same evidence; it would not fix the coverage line naming Nimbrel first). current_treatment is not proposed separately: the nimbrel line already says it is the standard advanced therapy most patients use. insurance_coverage and pipeline were often never released, but no grading shows a recommendation hurt by their absence, so neither is proposed.
